'''Vortex''' was a [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Glythe sector/Legends|Glythe sector]]. The planet was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Vor]]s, a non-emotional winged species.

==Description==
[[File:Vor_dwellings.png|thumb|left|170px|[[Vor]] dwellings on Vortex.]]
Vortex was known for its violent weather, particularly sharp winds, which was caused by an abnormal tilt in the planet's axis. During the winter [[Standard month/Legends|months]], vast polar ice caps formed almost instantaneously by the freezing [[Gas/Legends|gases]] in the planet's [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]]. The sudden change in air pressure made huge currents, which swept across the entire planet.

==History==
The only [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] that evolved in Vortex was known as the [[Vor]]s.<ref name="JASB" /><ref name="EGP" />

Vortex joined the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] in [[3977 BBY]].

The center of the Vor's society was the [[Cathedral of Winds/Legends|Cathedral of Winds]], a building that resonated with tones as the planet's strong winds struck it. [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Ackbar]] crashed his modified [[B-wing/E starfighter|B-wing]] into the Cathedral, due to sabotage by double-agent [[Terpfen]]. The Vors, apparently unconcerned despite the tragic loss of life, rebuilt the cathedral in a new design. At that point [[Krini-shen]] was the Chief Council.

The planet was represented in the [[New Republic Senate/Legends|New Republic Senate]] by [[Fyg Boras]].

The [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Battle of the Ten Tempests system|conquered]] Vortex few times after the [[Battle of Fondor]], in [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]].<ref name="TNJOS" /><ref name="TEA" /> A [[Battle near Vortex|minor engagement]] occurred near Vortex shortly before the [[Battle of Coruscant (Yuuzhan Vong War)|Fall of Coruscant]].<ref name="SbS">''[[The New Jedi Order: Star by Star]]''</ref> Near the end of the war, the [[Ryn Network]] operated a cell on the world.
